# FlashAlpha Historical Java SDK

> Java client for the FlashAlpha Historical API — point-in-time replay
> of every live FlashAlpha analytics endpoint. Ask what GEX, gamma
> flip, VRP, narrative, max pain, exposure levels, or the full stock
> summary looked like at any minute back to **2017-01-03**, in the
> exact same response shape as the live API.

## What FlashAlpha is

FlashAlpha (https://flashalpha.com) is an options dealer-flow
analytics platform. The **Historical** API replays the same analytics
that the live API exposes — for any timestamp in coverage. Same
response shapes, same field names, same semantics.

Interactive playground (live + historical): https://lab.flashalpha.com/swagger.

## What this SDK provides

- `FlashAlphaHistoricalClient` — thin HTTP wrapper. Methods accept
  an `at` parameter (string, `LocalDateTime`, or `LocalDate`) and
  return `com.google.gson.JsonObject`. Date-only `at` snaps to
  16:00 ET on the API side.
- `Backtester` and `Replay` helpers — iterate days or minutes and
  collect per-step responses for backtests / event studies.
- Strongly-typed response POCOs for the highest-ROI endpoints —
  `ExposureSummaryResponse`, `MaxPainResponse`, `VrpResponse`,
  `StockSummaryResponse`, `NarrativeResponse`,
  `ExposureLevelsResponse`.
- Typed exception hierarchy: `AuthenticationException`,
  `TierRestrictedException`, `InvalidAtException`, `NoDataException`,
  `SymbolNotFoundException`, `NoCoverageException`,
  `InsufficientDataException`, `RateLimitException`,
  `ServerException`, `FlashAlphaHistoricalException`.

## Data provenance

Every response carries two objects in the same shape. `archive_as_of` is the vintage of
the archive rows actually replayed for the timestamp requested - equity and index spot,
their option chains, futures and futures options, the classified trade tape, settled open
interest, and the macro series, each reported separately because they are stored and
replayed independently. `data_as_of` is the live-feed counterpart and reports `null` for every feed here,
because a replay node reads the archive and consumes no live feed; it is still returned so
the envelope has one shape across the live and historical services, and so a historical
response cannot be mistaken for a live one. `endpoint_version` identifies the deployment.

`archive_as_of` is what makes an archive gap detectable. Request a moment with no row and
the query returns the most recent earlier row; nothing else in the response distinguishes
the two. Point-in-time work should read it and drop or flag observations whose inputs
precede the requested instant by more than the study tolerates. `oi_feed` trailing by a
session is correct rather than a gap: settled open interest is published once per session,
so the newest figure that existed at any intraday moment is the prior close. Every response
model extends `FlashAlphaResponse`, so all three are typed members. Full reference:
https://flashalpha.com/docs/lab-api-overview#response-envelope

## Key endpoints

All accept an `at` parameter alongside the live signature.

- `/v1/exposure/summary/{symbol}` — full GEX / DEX / VEX / CHEX,
  gamma flip, regime, hedging estimate, 0DTE share at `at`.
- `/v1/exposure/levels/{symbol}` — minimal key-levels view at `at`.
- `/v1/exposure/zero-dte/{symbol}` — same-day-expiration deep dive
  at `at`.
- `/v1/exposure/narrative/{symbol}` — verbal output at `at`.
- `/v1/maxpain/{symbol}` — max pain + pin probability at `at`.
- `/v1/vrp/{symbol}` — variance risk premium at `at`.
- `/v1/stock/{symbol}/summary` — full one-shot dashboard at `at`.
- `/v1/volatility/{symbol}` and `/v1/adv_volatility/{symbol}` —
  vol term structure, surface, VRP at `at`.

## Tier (summary)

- **Alpha plan** is required for every historical endpoint. The same
  `X-Api-Key` you use against `api.flashalpha.com` works against the
  historical host once your account is on Alpha+.

Sign up at https://flashalpha.com. Playground:
https://lab.flashalpha.com/swagger.
